key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films are not just defects—they are chemically validated failure nucleation sites that accelerate degradation at impurity–perovskite interfaces.
engineering_relevance: A fast, non-invasive microscopy-plus-ML screening workflow can pre-qualify perovskite films in seconds, helping scale stable tandem solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Nano-FTIR spectroscopy to chemically identify impurity phases
High-resolution reflected-light microscopy for rapid, non-invasive imaging
Machine learning image analysis to detect and quantify harmful impurities
evidence_signal: Photo-stress and tracking experiments showed degradation begins at impurity interfaces, and films with higher impurity density degraded faster early on, supporting impurity density as an early-warning stability metric.
watch_item: The screening metric should be validated across broader perovskite compositions, processing routes, and imaging setups before routine manufacturing deployment.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
